os_version: 5.11 (Final), userland of the PyPA image quay.io/pypa/manylinux1_x86_64 (glibc 2.5)
environment_detail: A DOCKER CONTAINER, NOT A CENTOS 5 MACHINE. The lowest Linux userland tried by the project (owner's request of 2026-11-15, after the manylinux2010 run: an older userland than CentOS 6.10; success here counts for newer systems; no other distribution, no i686, no ARM). The userland is the PyPA image quay.io/pypa/manylinux1_x86_64 (digest sha256:506d34897aa3e6f41297bb05e721f92b6cebd23966b5c3a36b015ec7ba5c764d, created 2024-04-29, 1.58 GB) with the changes of tools/trials/linux-manylinux1-x86_64/Dockerfile: CentOS release 5.11 (Final), glibc 2.5-123.el5_11.3, libstdc++ 4.1.2-55.el5 (GLIBCXX_3.4 at most), libX11 1.0.3-11.el5_7.1, libXft 2.1.10-1.1, fontconfig 2.4.1-7.el5, freetype 2.2.1-32.el5_9.1, xorg-x11-server-Xvfb 1.1.1-48.107.el5.centos (the X server of every run, a private display :99 or :98 or :97, 1280x1024x24, never the WSLg display; run through a wrapper that adds a font path, see below), DejaVu LGC fonts 2.10 and Bitstream Vera, the misc and Type1 X fonts; compiler devtoolset-2 gcc/g++ 4.8.2 20140120 (Red Hat 4.8.2-15) (-std=c++11 accepted, no warning with -Wall -Wextra -pedantic), cmake 3.22.6 (NOT the image's: it has none; the pip wheel 'cmake<3.23', manylinux1 build, installed into its Python 3.8), GNU make 3.81, Python 3.8.19 from /opt/python/cp38-cp38 for tools/build.py (the system Python of CentOS 5 is 2.4.3). The container runs on Docker Desktop 29.8.0 (engine linux/amd64) on the Windows 11 host of windows-11-x64 (WSL2 backend), so the KERNEL IS NOT THE CENTOS 5 ONE: it is the Microsoft WSL2 kernel 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 shared with the host (uname -r in the container), on an Intel Core i5-8300H (x86_64). What this proves is the USERLAND floor: a binary built by that compiler against glibc 2.5 and its libraries loads and runs with them. What it does not prove: a real CentOS 5 kernel (2.6.18), a CentOS 5 boot, a real Xorg server, a window manager, a desktop or a real keyboard (the X server is Xvfb 1.1.1, itself a CentOS 5 package). THE IMAGE RUNS UNMODIFIED ONLY ON A KERNEL THAT MAPS THE VSYSCALL PAGE: glibc 2.5 reads the time through the fixed vsyscall page (0xffffffffff600000 and 0xffffffffff600400), which the default WSL2 kernel does not map (vsyscall=none), so on that default bash, perl, python3, yum, cc1 and getaddrinfo die with SIGSEGV (exit 139); the owner enabled vsyscall=emulate in the kernel command line of WSL2 (/proc/cmdline of the container ends with vsyscall=emulate), and with it the unmodified CentOS 5.11 libc (glibc-2.5-123.el5_11.3, rpm -V clean) runs everything. A first run of the same day used an image whose libc was patched at its two call sites to run on the default kernel; the same results came out and the patch was removed. Two workarounds remain, both in the Dockerfile and none in the product: (1) Xvfb 1.1.1 needs xorg-x11-server-utils for rgb.txt (without it no colour name resolves, XftColorAllocName fails and the UI silently falls back to the core font: a run in that state was in fact the core-font path and was discarded) and, started without a font path, waits 2 to 5 seconds for the font server unix/:7100 at the first font (display_ms 2,000 to 5,000 against about 20): /usr/local/bin/Xvfb is a wrapper that adds -fp with the misc and Type1 directories; (2) the image has no CMake, hence the pip wheel. Build and run happened inside the container; the worktree was mounted at /src and the build directory was a Docker volume mounted as /root/loomora-build, outside the repository. The yum repositories were already pointed at http://archive.kernel.org/centos-vault/5.11/ by the image (http only: the CentOS 5 TLS stack is far too old for https); the libselinux repository of the image (a centosplus build of libselinux) had to be enabled and the 32-bit packages excluded for yum to resolve.
eol_source: CentOS 5 reached end of life on 2017-03-31 (CentOS Project; its last release is 5.11, 2014-09-29, and its repositories moved to vault.centos.org; the first CentOS 5 release is 2007-04-12). The Linux end-of-life test of the backend (loomora_is_eol) looks at the kernel release from uname, and the container reports the WSL2 kernel 6.18, which is not end of life: so eol_warning_shown is false in the probe lines of this platform although the distribution is end of life. The banner is not shown by this system (the kernel is the host's).
kernel: 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 (uname -srm in the container: Linux 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64), the kernel of the Docker Desktop and WSL2 VM, not a CentOS 5 kernel (2.6.18)
glibc: 2.5 (glibc-2.5-123.el5_11.3, unmodified; ldd --version: ldd (GNU libc) 2.5; needs a kernel with vsyscall=emulate or a real CentOS 5 kernel)
compiler: gcc/g++ 4.8.2 20140120 (Red Hat 4.8.2-15), devtoolset-2 of the image, -std=c++11, GNU ld 2.23.52.0.1-10.el5, libstdc++ of the system 4.1.2 (the UI needs GLIBCXX_3.4 and CXXABI_1.3 only); cmake 3.22.6 (pip wheel), GNU make 3.81 (Unix Makefiles, no Ninja), Python 3.8.19 (/opt/python/cp38-cp38)
hardware: The host of windows-11-x64: MSI GL63 8RD, Intel Core i5-8300H (x86_64), 8 logical CPUs; the container has no CPU limit set
release_date_source: CentOS 5.11 release date 2014-09-29 (CentOS Project release announcement; the first CentOS 5 release is 5.0, 2007-04-12, which was NOT tried: the record is dated from the system actually run, 5.11); age_years = days from 2014-09-29 to the trial date 2026-11-15 divided by 365.25. is_floor is true for the Linux Legacy UI only: it is the lowest Linux system tried and the one that decides the Linux Legacy floor of the PoC; the Linux Modern UI was not tried on it (verdict linux-centos-5.11-x86_64-modern, not_tested).
floor_note: The floor of the Linux Legacy UI for the PoC since 2026-11-15 (confirmed by the owner): the lowest Linux userland tried, the manylinux1 container (CentOS 5.11 userland, glibc 2.5, unmodified), which supersedes the manylinux2010 container (linux-centos-6.10-x86_64, CentOS 6.10, glibc 2.12, whose verdict is kept). Floor of the userland, not of the kernel (the container uses the WSL2 kernel 6.18, started with vsyscall=emulate so that glibc 2.5 runs). The Linux Modern UI was not tried on it.
